request.instructions: flips when turning at high speeds

changes.reason: Lowering the center of mass slightly and biasing it a bit rearward helps prevent rollovers during fast turns.
More downforce improves high-speed stability and reduces flipping tendency.
Higher anti-roll stiffness helps keep the car planted in cornering.
A small front bias supports stability without making the car skatey.
Slightly reducing steering lock makes the vehicle less likely to tip at speed.
A modest front brake bias helps keep the chassis settled under braking.

Windows folder metadata file; not used by the importer and not executable.
